text.p: These are the leading stories in the Beirut press on Friday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
-Prime Minister Hariri visited Damascus. Parliament Speaker Berri went there again. Artificial coalition in the Bekaa's pro-government list.
-U.S. ambassador Jones visited the foreign ministry twice in 24 hours. He said the region was passing through a transitional period.
-Israeli warplanes flew over Beirut and Baalbek.
-Some 409,955 voters to chose among 142 candidates in the last round of voting in Bekaa on Sunday.

-Acting Finance Minister Siniora discussed with the ambassadors of Canada and China means of supporting Lebanon in the consultative committee formed under the terms of an April ceasefire understanding that put an end to a 17-day Israeli blitz on Lebanon.
-A $70 million disagreement between Ericsson and the Lebanese ministry of posts and telecommunications.
-The government to reopen the issue of organising the audiovisual media next week.
-Beirut is taking seriously a warning by Israel's proxy militia in south Lebanon of a big Israeli military operation in Lebanon.
